THE PROBLEM WE’RE SOLVING

Trading and agents.
Without a maze
of gas tokens.

Users and agents moving between networks face separate native gas balances, funding steps and fee rules. Trading adds another layer: research, execution and payment evidence need to stay connected.

Our goal is one shared MGAS account for network fees and useful services, with sponsors paying each chain’s native gas. The current prototype connects trading research to prepaid service credits and a managed Arc USDC report workflow. Shared-credit gas execution is the next stage.

01

One gas balance for agent wallets

Base tMGAS currently funds one service-credit account. The broader gas solution will reserve a reviewed MGAS fee, dispatch through a funded network sponsor, and reconcile the actual native cost and service markup.

02

Arc and USDC as the proposed settlement backbone

The Circle grant proposal puts Arc USDC settlement behind agent-service purchases and a future gas-funding route. This connects the single-token gas vision to useful trading and payment tools.

Base-funded MGAS account through these two report services.

01 ↗
RESEARCH

Know what trading costs.

A historical backtest report with fees, slippage, drawdown and identical-data comparisons for baseline, zero-cost and higher-cost scenarios. Spot simulation at 1×; no live trading.

Frozen inputs · Actual calculations · No profit promise
0.055MGAS credits / report0.050 base + 0.005 markup
02 ≋
PAYMENT EVIDENCE

Find out what settled.

A transaction check that separates confirmed, failed, pending and missing outcomes, reports native fees, and checks expected EVM token transfers when the asset is specified.

Five test networks · Evidence over assumptions
0.011MGAS credits / report0.010 base + 0.001 markup

These Base-funded services add zero chain gas. Prices include a 10% markup on the base service price. Funding carries its own separately reviewed tMGAS gas charge. The separate managed Arc report preview prices backtests at 0.055 test USDC and transaction checks at 0.011, with signed agent budgets and matching payment/delivery receipts. Its live wallet proof is pending. Test credits have no cash value. Agent controls and Arc report details ↗

Three local agent skills guide a 15-tool keyless MCP preview. Optional OpenAI chat has separate Arc and read-only Solana modes, with three tools per mode. This public repository contains the website, not the private platform. npm and official MCP Registry publication remain pending.

MCP / EXAMPLE REQUEST
// Local Arc testnet tool call

  payer: "<buyer public EVM address>",
  maxAmountRaw: "11000",
  requestKey: "arc_service_pilot_0001"
})

// Owner opens the returned reviewUrl.
// Buyer authorizes; seller signs its proof.
// Poll the SAME request ID.

matex_gas_arc_get_payment({
  id: "<returned request id>"
})

PROPOSED GRANT WORK

A roadmap you
can hold us to.

Proposed milestones for discussion.
Scope and funding are subject to review.

01

FIRST PROOF

Arc settlement, end to end.

Complete owner-approved USDC/x402 purchases on Arc testnet. Publish reproducible evidence, matching receipts and MCP-delivered results.

Acceptance: public testnet receipts + reproducible checks
02

USEFUL COMMERCE

Connect trading utility to Arc.

Connect real backtest and reconciliation reports to Arc USDC settlement, then link agent-wallet actions to the trading workspace. Keep service fees separate from trading capital and define MGAS accounting explicitly.

Acceptance: one payment → one delivered report → one receipt
03

SAFER OPERATIONS

Pilot one-balance gas sponsorship.

Fund and verify a bounded network sponsor, charge an owner-reviewed MGAS fee, reconcile native gas plus the disclosed markup, and add the access controls, refunds and independent review needed before broader execution.

Acceptance: native gas receipt + matching MGAS accounting + reviewed controls
04

DEVELOPER VALIDATION

Prove it with external builders.

Run a small developer pilot. Publish completed purchases, failures, repeat use and integration feedback. Use observed demand to guide a controlled production plan.

Acceptance: published pilot outcomes, including failures
